name: Musée National du Burkina Faso
funding: State museum (EPSCT) with 30,000+ visits Jan-Oct 2024, funded by the culture ministry plus Ouagadougou commune, Agence Faso Mɛbo and unnamed company donors.
watch: Its director says partners rarely back museums. A friends' association started a donation drive in April 2026.
records_note: Documents page is empty and no accounts or funders are posted; the site says a board exists under a 2002 decree but names no one.

name: Musée National du Cameroun
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Arts and Culture; €1M modernisation from AFD via debt-swap C2D (2019-24), Phase 2 2025-27, run by Expertise France.
watch: National museum in the former presidential palace since 1988. Its modernisation is funded by French debt conversion.
records_note: It has no site of its own found and publishes no reports, accounts, funder list or board; its funders appear only on AFD project pages.

name: Musée National du Mali
funding: State museum with 10,937 visitors in 2025, run by Mali's culture ministry; Spain's AECID backs the 2026 'Repenser le Musée' project (amount undisclosed).
watch: EU paid for its 2002 extension. In April 2026 Spain launched a project for training, conservation and outreach.
records_note: No annual reports, accounts, funder list or board on the museum's old site; its web address now redirects to an unrelated site.

name: Musée Public National d'Art Moderne et Contemporain (MAMA)
funding: Public body (EPA) under the Ministry of Culture since 2007, with little budget beyond its opening; collection built mostly from private and artist donations.
watch: In a 1909 neo-Moorish department store on rue Larbi Ben M'hidi; opened for Algiers Capital of Arab Culture 2007.
records_note: Its old site, now offline, showed no reports, accounts, funder list or board in an archived copy; only mission, publications and a support link.

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
funding: Opened 2017, paid for by Pierre Bergé's 2015 sale of Moroccan art and run on Jardin Majorelle ticket income (700k+ visitors a year); a luxury-fashion legacy.
watch: Run by the Fondation Jardin Majorelle (president Madison Cox) next to the garden; it shares the site's 700k+ visitors.
records_note: The museum site and the Jardin Majorelle site publish no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; the parent foundation's own site returned unreadable code.

name: Musée Boribana
funding: Founded with private money by Boubacar Koné and actress CCH Pounder; Koné gave it to the Senegalese state in December 2014.
watch: Ngor museum of contemporary African art with artist studios and a residency. A conservator from the Ministry of Culture took office in March 2015.
records_note: The ministry page on Boribana gives its history and 2014 state handover but no budget, reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara (MuCAT)
funding: Built on the initiative of Adama Toungara, then mayor of Abobo; the director says it was built from own funds.
watch: Stands opposite Abobo town hall on 3,500 m², designed by architect Issa Diabaté. Opened with the pan-African show Prête-moi ton rêve.
records_note: MuCAT's site lists a team but no board, partners, reports or accounts; it says the museum is private, foundation-owned and gets no state subsidy.

name: Museion
funding: Autonomous Province of Bolzano, plus members and exhibition sponsors.
records_note: No annual report; the foundation's transparency portal posts annual accounts 2022 to 2025 and its six-member board, while partners appear as undated logos.

name: Museo de Antioquia
funding: Ministerio de las Culturas, Alcaldía de Medellín, Área Metropolitana; aliados include EPM, Bancolombia, SURA, Mineros, Metro de Medellín, Comfama and the Chamber of Commerce.
records_note: Shows a page of allies as undated logos with alt text, and publishes no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Puerto Rico
funding: Non-profit (EIN 66-0420190); 2026 funders: NEA, IMLS, Luce, Wallace, Teiger, Banco Popular, Walmart, PR Tourism Co., The Macallan.
watch: Its funders include alcohol (The Macallan), retail (Walmart) and bank (Banco Popular) money. No controversy found.
records_note: Form 990 filings for 2020 to 2024 are on ProPublica; its sponsorship page shows three undated logos, and its board and team pages return 404.

name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago
watch: Two sites: Parque Forestal and Quinta Normal.
records_note: Posts none of its own; parent University of Chile posts a 2014-2018 report, budgets and execution reports, and a Consejo Universitario list.

name: Museo de Arte Costarricense (MAC)
funding: Ministry of Culture museum with a 2021 budget of about COLONES 1.77bn (about US$3M), 48% of it salaries; about 37,000 visitors in 2018.
watch: Public collection museum in La Sabana. Its board approved lending works to the presidential offices in Sep 2026 without saying which works.
records_note: The MAC posts leadership reports for 2018 to 2022, budget and execution reports, and board minutes, but no funder list or board roster.
